frequency_question: What is the historical frequency of successful successor treaty signings before the expiration of a foundational water-sharing agreement in the region?
membership_rule: Includes formal bilateral water-sharing treaties or major operational amendments between India and co-riparian neighbors (Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal) facing sunset clauses. Excludes unratified memoranda of intent.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty implementation and subsequent permanent Indus Commission persistence
Mahakali Treaty between India and Nepal
Teesta River interim water sharing agreement attempt

coverage_note: 4 named; represents the complete set of major formal river treaty negotiations between India and its immediate partition-linked neighbors in modern history.
known_gaps: Sub-national state-level water sharing pacts (e.g., Cauvery or Mahadayi within India) are excluded as they lack international sovereignty friction.
skeleton: Four major water diplomacy episodes in the region involving India and immediate neighbors, resulting in 3 successes and 1 failure.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 4 historical comparable episodes yields a raw base rate of 75 percent, adjusted for political turbulence.
validity_reason: Bilateral hydro-diplomacy norms in South Asia evolve slowly over decades, anchored by strategic necessity and institutional bureaucracy.
